role: external oracle for the electric near field inside a patterned layer with a curved wall: a 3D finite-element field of a dielectric cylinder, which the windowed split reconstruction and the plain Fourier sum are measured against

references.build: FEniCS (dolfin) 2019.1 underneath, gmsh for the geometry and the mesh, MUMPS direct solve out of core

modified.description: used through its public Python API; the package itself was not changed

references.settings: Maxwell3DPeriodic on one eighth of the cell, using the exact mirror symmetries of normal incidence with E along x (the x mirror a perfect electric wall, the y mirror a perfect magnetic wall, and an even/odd split in z, two solves); second-order edge (Nedelec) elements; perfectly matched layers above and below; relative residual of the two direct solves 3.0e-12 and 2.3e-12; R = 0.024309 and T = 0.975554 from the same solution. The stored phasors are in gyptis's time convention, the conjugate of Wavebit's; the consumer maps them as -exp(2 pi i h / wavelength) * conj(E), with h the layer thickness
references.discretization: tetrahedral mesh graded toward the cylinder wall and its rims, 94078 cells and 621968 complex unknowns per solve, smallest edge 2.41 nm; the product side is a Fourier truncation of the same cell

generator.command: python fem_cyl.py c100_T4 c100 T4 12.25 1 (the finite-element run), then the plane samples laid out on the 48 x 48 grid

cost.note: both solves, factorization out of core

cell.centre: the cylinder axis is the cell centre

samples.plane: mid-height of the layer, z = 75 nm above its lower face
samples.layout: E[j, i, component] at (x[i], y[j]), components (Ex, Ey, Ez)

outcomes.reference_self_check: the next coarser mesh level (53246 cells) differs from this one by 0.11% of the plane RMS of the in-plane field over the same 2304 samples, and by 2.0% of it at the worst sample and component; R moves from 0.024314 to 0.024309

sources.references[0]: the run script, its log and the statistics stored with the run, read on 2026-11-14
sources.references[0].independence: the finite-element script imports numpy, dolfin, gmsh, gyptis and a NumPy-only module of sample points
